reason: The iron-bearing fraction must be separated from the screened regolith before processing, but the available equipment does not make the method obvious.
expectation: The inspection should identify an available way to separate or prepare the feedstock.

effect: The screened regolith has no currently available partners, so another piece of equipment must be prepared first.
reaction: I am curious how the magnetic separation will be set up.
reason: The materials retort is central to making iron, so inspecting it may reveal the required preparation.
expectation: The inspection should show what can be fitted to or used with the retort.

effect: The retort is now fed with hydrogen and ready for concentrate, but the magnetic fraction still needs separating.
reaction: The automatic connection clarified how the furnace and hydrogen supply work together.
reason: The power cable and steel may make an electromagnet for separating the iron-bearing fraction; this is a guess based on the stated need.
expectation: They may form a magnetic separator for the screened regolith.

effect: The cable and steel made a powered separator, providing the missing way to prepare the iron-bearing feedstock.
reaction: The switchable electromagnet makes the separation method clear.
reason: The separator should extract the magnetic fraction from the screened regolith.
expectation: The magnet will collect an iron-bearing concentrate for the retort.

effect: The separator produced the iron-rich concentrate needed by the hydrogen-fed retort.
reaction: The distinction between a magnetic assay and merely red soil is useful.
reason: The prepared concentrate belongs in the hydrogen-fed retort for processing.
expectation: The retort will heat and reduce the concentrate to produce iron.

effect: The retort produced porous reduced iron, which still needs forming into usable metal.
reaction: The explanation makes the hydrogen reduction and the sponge's weakness clear.
reason: The protected carrier brings the iron sponge to the press, making that the clear next step.
expectation: The press will consolidate the porous iron into a usable form.

effect: The heated press consolidated the iron into a dense billet, and the next goal is to make a process frame.
reaction: The distinction between consolidating and shaping the iron is useful.
reason: The billet needs shaping into a frame; the workshop press is the most plausible available equipment for that.
expectation: The press may shape the billet into components for the process frame.

effect: The press shaped the billet into bars and brackets suitable for a non-pressure frame.
reaction: The distinction between supports and flight hardware makes their intended use clearer.
reason: The bars and brackets should form the process frame on the prepared fuel-fab footing.
expectation: The iron supports will be assembled into a process frame at the industrial site.

effect: The bars and brackets became a process frame on the footing, completing the chapter's goals.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the local iron become a practical support for the gas installation.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making and using the electromagnet was most worthwhile: it connected a plausible construction to magnetic separation, and the assay explanation clarified why red colour alone was not enough to identify suitable feedstock.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the screened regolith yielded no partners, so it did little to clarify the missing preparation.

surprise.text: Inspecting the retort automatically connected it to the hydrogen outlet; I had expected only compatibility information.

arbitrary.text: The choice to combine a power cable with steel was a guess: the need for magnetic separation suggested an electromagnet, but the available pieces did not make that recipe certain.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the locally made frame supports the return-fuel installation, especially after the chapter explained the limits of the iron parts.
